readings.title: Saul the Benjamite
readings.subtitle: The Search for Donkeys Leads to a Kingdom
readings.text: [1 Samuel 9:1] And there was a man of Binyamin whose name was Qish, son of Aḇi’ĕl, son of Tseror, son of Bekorath, son of Aphiah, a Binyamite, a mighty man of power. [2] And he had a son whose name was Sha’ul, young and handsome. And there was not a more handsome man than he among the children of Yisra’ĕl – taller than any of the people from his shoulders upwards. [3] And the donkeys of Qish, Sha’ul’s father, were lost. And Qish said to his son Sha’ul, “Please take <dn>את</dn> one of the servants with you, and arise, go look for <dn>את</dn> the donkeys.” [4] And he passed through the mountains of Ephrayim and passed through the land of Shalishah, but they did not find them. Then they passed through the land of Sha‛alim, and they were not there. Then he passed through the land of the Binyamites, but they did not find them. [5] When they had come to the land of Tsuph, Sha’ul said to his servant who was with him, “Come, let us turn back, lest my father stop thinking about the donkeys and become worried about us.” [6] And he said to him, “See, please, there is a man of <dn>Elohim</dn> in this city, and the man is held in esteem. All that he says comes true without fail. Now, let us go there. It could be that he shows us <dn>את</dn> the way to go.” [7] And Sha’ul said to his servant, “But look, if we go, what do we bring the man? For the bread in our vessels is all gone, and there is no present to bring to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>. What do we have?” [8] And the servant answered Sha’ul again and said, “Look, I have here at hand one-fourth of a sheqel of silver. And I shall give that to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and he shall tell us <dn>את</dn> our way.” [9] (Formerly in Yisra’ĕl, when a man went to inquire of <dn>Elohim</dn>, he spoke thus, “Come, let us go to the seer,” for the prophet of today was formerly called a seer.) [10] And Sha’ul said to his servant, “Good is your word. Come, let us go.” And they went to the city where the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> was. [11] As they were going up the hill to the city, they met young women going out to draw water, and said to them, “Is the seer here?” [12] And they answered them and said, “He is. See, he is ahead of you. Hurry now, for today he came to this city, because there is a slaughtering for the people today on the high place. [13] “As soon as you come into the city, you shall find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. For the people do not eat until he comes, because he blesses the slaughtering. Afterward those who are invited eat. And now, go up, for you shall find him about this time.” [14] And they went up to the city. As they were coming into the city, see, Shemu’ĕl was coming out toward them to go up to the high place. [15] Now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had uncovered <dn>את</dn> the ear of Shemu’ĕl one day before Sha’ul came, saying, [16] <dq>“At this time tomorrow I send you a man from the land of Binyamin, and you shall anoint him leader over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and he shall save <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon <dn>My</dn> people, because their cry has come to <dn>Me</dn>.”</dq> [17] And when Shemu’ĕl saw <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“See the man of whom <dn>I</dn> spoke to you. This one is to restrain <dn>My</dn> people.”</dq> [18] And Sha’ul drew near to <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl in the gate, and said, “Please tell me, where is the seer’s house?” [19] And Shemu’ĕl answered <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul and said, “I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today. And tomorrow I shall let you go and make known to you all that is in your heart. [20] “And as for your donkeys that were lost three days ago, do not set <dn>את</dn> your heart on them, for they have been found. And on whom is all the desire of Yisra’ĕl? Is it not on you and on all your father’s house?” [21] And Sha’ul answered and said, “Am I not a Binyamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and my clan the least of all the clans of the tribe of Binyamin? Why then do you speak like this to me?” [22] And Shemu’ĕl took <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> his servant and brought them into the hall, and gave them a place at the head of those who were invited, and they were about thirty men. [23] And Shemu’ĕl said to the cook, “Bring <dn>את</dn> the portion which I gave you, of which I said to you, ‘Set it apart.’ ” [24] And the cook brought out <dn>את</dn> the thigh and that which was on it, and set it before Sha’ul. And Shemu’ĕl said, “See what was kept back. It was set before you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for this appointed time, saying, ‘I have invited the people.’ ” So Sha’ul ate with Shemu’ĕl that day. [25] And they came down from the high place into the city, and he spoke with Sha’ul on the roof. [26] And they rose early. And it came to be, about the break of day, that Shemu’ĕl called to Sha’ul on the roof, saying, “Rise, so that I send you away.” And Sha’ul rose, and both of them went out, he and Shemu’ĕl. [27] As they were going down to the outskirts of the city, Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “Say to the servant to go on ahead of us” – and he went on – “but you stand here a moment, so that I let you hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>Elohim</dn>.”

readings.title: The Anointing of Saul
readings.subtitle: Three Signs of Confirmation
readings.text: [1 Samuel 10:1] Then Shemu’ĕl took <dn>את</dn> a flask of oil and poured it on his head, and kissed him and said, “Is it not because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has anointed you leader over <dn>His</dn> inheritance? [2] “When you leave me today, you shall find two men by Raḥĕl’s tomb in the border of Binyamin at Tseltsah, and they shall say to you, ‘The donkeys which you went to look for have been found. And see, your father has left <dn>את</dn> the matters of the donkeys and is worrying about you, saying, “What shall I do for my son?” ’ [3] “And you shall go on further from there and come to the terebinth tree of Taḇor. And three men going up to <dn>Elohim</dn> at Bĕyth Ěl shall find you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a jar of wine. [4] “And they shall ask you of your peace, and give you two loaves of bread, which you receive from their hands. [5] “After that you go to the hill of <dn>Elohim</dn> where the Philistine watchtower is. And it shall be, when you have come there to the city, that you shall meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place with a stringed instrument, and a tambourine, and a flute, and a lyre before them, and they are prophesying. [6] “And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall come upon you, and you shall prophesy with them and be turned into another man. [7] “And it shall be, when these signs come to you, do for yourself what your hand finds to do, for <dn>Elohim</dn> is with you. [8] “And you shall go down before me to Gilgal, and see, I am coming down to you to offer burnt offerings and to make peace offerings. Wait seven days, till I come to you and show you <dn>את</dn> what you should do.”

readings.title: Is Saul Among the Prophets?
readings.subtitle: A Changed Heart
readings.text: [1 Samuel 10:9] And it came to be, when he had turned his back to go from Shemu’ĕl, that <dn>Elohim</dn> gave him another heart. And all those signs came on that day. [10] And they came there to the hill, and saw a group of prophets to meet him. And the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon him, and he prophesied in their midst. [11] And it came to be, all who knew him formerly looked, and saw that he prophesied among the prophets. So the people said to each other, “What is this that has come upon the son of Qish? Is Sha’ul also among the prophets?” [12] And a man there answered and said, “And who is their father?” Therefore it became a proverb: “Is Sha’ul also among the prophets?” [13] And when he had finished prophesying, he went to the high place. [14] And Sha’ul’s uncle said to him and his servant, “Where did you go?” And he said, “To look for the donkeys. And when we saw that they were nowhere, we went to Shemu’ĕl.” [15] And Sha’ul’s uncle said, “Please tell me what Shemu’ĕl said to you.” [16] And Sha’ul said to his uncle, “He informed us plainly that the donkeys had been found.” But about <dn>את</dn> the matter of the reign, of which Shemu’ĕl had spoken, he did not tell him.

readings.title: The Proclamation at Mizpah
readings.subtitle: The King Hidden in the Baggage
readings.text: [1 Samuel 10:17] And Shemu’ĕl called <dn>את</dn> the people together to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at Mitspah, [18] and said to the children of Yisra’ĕl, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl up out of Mitsrayim, and delivered you from the hand of the Mitsrites and from the hand of all kingdoms and of those who oppressed you.’</dq> [19] <dq>“And today you have rejected <dn>את</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who <dn>Himself</dn> saved you out of all your evils and your distresses. And you have said to <dn>Him</dn>, ‘No, but set a king over us!’ And now, present yourselves before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by your tribes and by your clans.”</dq> [20] And Shemu’ĕl brought near <dn>את</dn> all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and the tribe of Binyamin was taken. [21] And he brought near <dn>את</dn> the tribe of Binyamin by their clans, and the clan of Matri was taken. And Sha’ul son of Qish was taken. And they sought him, but he could not be found. [22] And they asked again of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Has the man come here yet?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered, <dq>“See, he has hidden himself among the equipment.”</dq> [23] And they ran and brought him from there. And he stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than any of the people from his shoulders upwards. [24] And Shemu’ĕl said to all the people, “Do you see him whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has chosen, that there is no one like him among all the people?” And all the people shouted and said, “Let the king live!” [25] And Shemu’ĕl spoke to the people <dn>את</dn> the ruling of the reign, and wrote it in a book and placed it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Shemu’ĕl sent <dn>את</dn> all the people away, every man to his house. [26] And Sha’ul also went home to Giḇ‛ah. And with him went the brave men whose hearts <dn>Elohim</dn> had touched. [27] But the children of Beliya‛al said, “How does this one save us?” And they despised him, and brought him no presents. But he was as one deaf.

readings.title: The Salvation of Jabesh Gilead
readings.subtitle: The Kingdom Renewed at Gilgal
readings.text: [1 Samuel 11:1] And Naḥash the Ammonite came up and encamped against yaḇĕsh Gil‛aḏ. And all the men of yaḇĕsh said to Naḥash, “Make a covenant with us, and we shall serve you.” [2] And Naḥash the Ammonite answered them, “On this condition I make a covenant with you, that I gouge out all your right eyes, and bring reproach on all Yisra’ĕl.” [3] And the elders of yaḇĕsh said to him, “Leave us alone for seven days, so that we send messengers to all the borders of Yisra’ĕl. And then, if there is no one to save us, we shall come out to you.” [4] And the messengers came to Giḇ‛ah of Sha’ul and spoke <dn>את</dn> the words in the hearing of the people. And all the people lifted up <dn>את</dn> their voices and wept. [5] And see, Sha’ul was coming behind the herd from the field. And Sha’ul said, “What is the matter with the people that they weep?” And they related to him <dn>את</dn> the words of the men of yaḇĕsh. [6] And the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon Sha’ul mightily as he heard these words, and his wrath burned greatly. [7] And he took a yoke of cattle and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the borders of Yisra’ĕl by the hands of messengers, saying, “Whoever does not go out after Sha’ul and after Shemu’ĕl, let it be done thus to his cattle.” And the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> fell on the people, and they came out as one man. [8] And he mustered them in Bezeq, and the children of Yisra’ĕl were three hundred thousand, and the men of Yehuḏah thirty thousand. [9] And they said to the messengers who came, “Say this to the men of yaḇĕsh Gil‛aḏ, ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have help.’ ” Then the messengers came and reported it to the men of yaḇĕsh, and they rejoiced. [10] So the men of yaḇĕsh said, “Tomorrow we come out to you, and you shall do to us whatever is good in your eyes.” [11] And it came to be on the next day that Sha’ul put <dn>את</dn> the people in three companies. And they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch, and struck <dn>את</dn> Ammon until the heat of the day. And it came to be that those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together. [12] And the people said to Shemu’ĕl, “Who is he who said, ‘Shall Sha’ul reign over us?’ Bring the men, so that we put them to death.” [13] But Sha’ul said, “No man is put to death this day, for today <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has worked salvation in Yisra’ĕl.” [14] And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “Come, and let us go to Gilgal and renew the reign there.” [15] And all the people went to Gilgal, and there they set up <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul to reign before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Gilgal. And there they made peace offerings before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and there Sha’ul and all the men of Yisra’ĕl rejoiced greatly.

readings.title: Samuel’s Farewell Address
readings.subtitle: Thunder and Rain in Harvest
readings.text: [1 Samuel 12:1] And Shemu’ĕl said to all Yisra’ĕl, “Look, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and have set a king over you. [2] “And now, see, the king is walking before you. And I am old and grey-headed, and look, my sons are with you. And I have walked before you from my youth to this day. [3] “Here I am. Witness against me before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and before <dn>His</dn> anointed: <dn>את</dn> Whose ox have I taken, or <dn>את</dn> whose donkey have I taken, or <dn>את</dn> whom have I oppressed? <dn>את</dn> Whom have I abused, or from whose hand have I received any bribe with which to blind my eyes? – then I restore it to you.” [4] And they said, “You have not oppressed us or abused us, nor have you taken any from anyone’s hand.” [5] And he said to them, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is witness against you, and <dn>His</dn> anointed is witness this day, that you have not found any in my hand.” And they answered, “He is witness.” [6] And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “It is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who raised up <dn>את</dn> Mosheh and <dn>את</dn> Aharon, and who brought <dn>את</dn> your fathers up from the land of Mitsrayim. [7] “And now, stand still, so that I judge <dn>את</dn> you before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning <dn>את</dn> all the righteous acts of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> did to you and your fathers: [8] “When Ya‛aqoḇ had gone into Mitsrayim, and your fathers cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> Mosheh and <dn>את</dn> Aharon, who brought <dn>את</dn> your fathers out of Mitsrayim and made them dwell in this place. [9] “But they forgot <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, so <dn>He</dn> sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Ḥatsor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the sovereign of Mo’aḇ, and they fought against them. [10] “And they cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and served <dn>את</dn> the Ba‛als and <dn>את</dn> the Ashtaroth. But now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we serve <dn>You</dn>.’ [11] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> Yerubba‛al, and <dn>את</dn> Beḏan, and <dn>את</dn> Yiphtaḥ, and <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and you dwelt in safety. [12] “And when you saw that Naḥash king of the children of Ammon came against you, you said to me, ‘No, but let a king reign over us,’ when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> was your sovereign. [13] “And now, see the king whom you have chosen, whom you have asked. And see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has set a king over you. [14] “If you fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and serve <dn>Him</dn>, and obey <dn>His</dn> voice, and do not rebel against <dn>את</dn> the command of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then both you and the king who reigns over you shall continue following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [15] “But if you do not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but rebel against <dn>את</dn> the command of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be against you, as it was against your fathers. [16] “And now, stand and see <dn>את</dn> this great matter which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does before your eyes: [17] “Is today not the wheat harvest? Let me call to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and let <dn>Him</dn> send thunder and rain, so that you know and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in asking for yourselves a king.” [18] So Shemu’ĕl called to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent thunder and rain that day. And all the people greatly feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ĕl. [19] And all the people said to Shemu’ĕl, “Pray for your servants to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, that we do not die, for we have added to all our sins the evil of asking for ourselves a king.” [20] And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “Do not fear. You have done <dn>את</dn> all this evil, yet do not turn aside from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with all your heart. [21] “And do not turn aside, for then you go after emptinesses which do not profit or deliver, for they are nothing. [22] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not going to forsake <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> people, for <dn>His</dn> great Name’s sake, because it has pleased <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to make <dn>את</dn> you <dn>His</dn> people. [23] “Also, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in ceasing to pray for you. But I shall teach <dn>את</dn> you <dn>את</dn> the good and straight way. [24] “Only fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and you shall serve <dn>Him</dn> in truth with all your heart, for see what great matters <dn>He</dn> has done for you. [25] “But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king are consumed.”
